title: Defined, implementation-defined, unspecified and undefined behaviour
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: Defined behaviour is specified by the C standard. Implementation-defined behaviour is selected and documented by an implementation. Unspecified behaviour permits one of several outcomes without requiring documentation. Undefined behaviour imposes no requirements on the implementation.
understand.whyItMatters: Distinguishing these categories is essential for portable reasoning and security. A program must not rely on undefined behaviour or confuse unspecified choices with documented implementation decisions.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

explain.narrative:
Defined behaviour is specified by the C standard. Implementation-defined behaviour is selected and documented by an implementation. Unspecified behaviour permits one of several outcomes without requiring documentation. Undefined behaviour imposes no requirements on the implementation.

State assumptions and constraints, consult the applicable standard or tool documentation, and verify the result with appropriate compiler diagnostics and tests. Separate portable guarantees from implementation-specific behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: Unsigned arithmetic is defined modulo one more than the maximum representable value. This differs from signed integer overflow, which is undefined when the mathematical result is not representable.

practise.guidedTask: Classify signed overflow, unsigned wraparound and a documented implementation-defined choice.
practise.independentTask: Review a short C program and label each behaviour category with the applicable standard rule.
hints: Undefined behaviour is not merely an unpredictable but otherwise valid result.
Implementation-defined behaviour should be documented by the implementation.
Do not infer a language guarantee from one compiler's observed output.
